issues.description: The 'url' field is set to an empty string with the comment '# CI fills this'. Code style rule §5 explicitly lists 'url = ""  # CI fills this' as a forbidden template placeholder. The adapter should fill in the recipe repository URL before merging.
issues.recommendation: Replace the empty url with the actual recipe repository URL (e.g., the conan repo URL on cnb.cool).

issues.rule: code-style.md §12 (conandata.yml 规范 / 补丁文件规范)
issues.description: The patch_description values do not follow the expected format 'NNNN description' (with 4-digit sequence number prefix). The code style example shows '0001 build aux config.guess' — descriptions should start with the patch sequence number. Current descriptions are: 'Add musl libc compatibility shims...', 'Include musl shim in list.h', etc.
issues.recommendation: Prefix each patch_description with the corresponding sequence number, e.g., '0001 add musl libc compatibility shims', '0002 include shim in list.h', etc.

issues.description: The test_package conanfile.py is missing the required shebang (#!/usr/bin/env python3) and docstring header. Code style rule §1 states conanfile.py must have a shebang + docstring. While this rule may be primarily intended for the main recipe conanfile.py, applying it to test_package conanfile.py would improve consistency.
issues.recommendation: Add '#!/usr/bin/env python3' and a brief docstring at the top of test_package/conanfile.py.

issues.description: The test_package only calls efi_get_libefivar_version() to check the library version number. While this is a valid smoke test for a library that requires EFI hardware for full functionality, it does not exercise any EFI variable read/write API. efivar is a system-level library (Rule R40: 系统底层), so deeper functional testing would be beneficial if test hardware is available. This is acceptable as a smoke test on non-EFI devices.
issues.recommendation: Consider adding tests that exercise more efivar APIs (e.g., efi_variable_alloc, efi_variable_set) with mocked or test EFI variables, if feasible on the target platform.

issues.description: The conanfile.py build() method does not include a platform guard such as 'if self.settings.os in ("Linux", "OHOS"):'. While the recipe builds unconditionally (which works for OHOS), adding an explicit platform guard would follow R32 best practices and prevent accidental builds on unsupported platforms.
issues.recommendation: Consider adding 'if self.settings.os not in ("Linux", "OHOS"): raise ConanInvalidConfiguration(...)' in configure() or build().
